question: The Italian company La Selvaggia di Bernardi Lorenzo has just been kicked out of the Conxemar exhibition in Vigo after it was revealed that pictures of naked women were used in its promotional catalogues.

Following the discovery of that sexist and despicable material in one of the company’s brochures, the question has arisen as to whether the Italian Government has misused EU funds, given that, according to public information, the company supposedly received more than EUR 128 000 in EU funds under an aid scheme for marketing and transformation. In light of this: 1.
Does the Commission consider the use of sexist images to be compatible with EU values and legislation?
Will it contact the Italian Government regarding the aid granted and investigate whether EU funds have been used to produce such abhorrent materials and, if so, require that they be repaid?
How will it ensure that the current and future EU budget does not fund initiatives that violate the integrity of women?
